note: HAND-WRITTEN. This file is the independent oracle for contract rule C2 — npm export resolution —
and it was written BEFORE the resolver existed. It is never generated by running Nerve, and no
script writes it. If it were produced by the thing it grades, the precision measurement over it
would be Nerve agreeing with itself, which is the exact failure a measured gate exists to prevent.
Every row below was read off fixtures/contracts-exports/host/src/app.ts and the seven package
manifests beside it, by hand. A C2 declaration is identified by the pair (importing file, import
specifier) — the two things that identify an import inside a repository — so `section` holds the
importing file's repository-relative path and `name` holds the specifier as written. Neither is a
line number, a link id or an entity id, because every one of those could only be obtained by
running the thing under test and keying on one would make this file a derived artifact.
The fixture is seven separate checkouts. `host` is the repository being scanned; `pkg-map`,
is a real Nerve repository that is deliberately NOT registered, so that 'a package a manifest
names' and 'a package Nerve may link to' stay distinguishable.
THIS TABLE IS NEVER SUMMED WITH C1's OR C3's. Three rules, three tables, no combined number.
evidence_chain: 1. this import specifier — written in host/src/app.ts and cached by indexing
2. this file: dependency — the specifier's package part must be a C1 dependency key in host/package.json
3. this name — the neighbour's own package.json must declare that package part as its `name`
4. this exports entry — the subpath must be named by the neighbour's own exports, or by module/main/types when it declares no exports

resolution_order.why: one documented order, applied at every nesting level. The cached specifier set does not distinguish an ESM import from a CJS require, so the ESM condition is preferred rather than guessed at per call site, and the condition actually taken is recorded on the link.

verdicts.link: this declaration must produce exactly one contract link per entry in `targets`, each to the named registry entry and each carrying the named form. Producing none is a false negative; producing one to another target is a false positive.
verdicts.unresolved: the syntax is supported and was read in full, and it reaches no file in a registered neighbour. It must produce NO link and must be reported with the named reason. A link here is a false positive.
verdicts.unsupported: the export shape is one Nerve declines to read. It must produce no link and must be tallied with the named form. A link here is a false positive; a silent drop is a defect even though it is not a false positive.
verdicts.declined_true_link: the neighbour's own exports map does name a real file for this specifier, and the form is outside the enumerated syntax. Nerve declines it, records it with the form named, and this file counts it as a FALSE NEGATIVE. That is 10b's `Views.handle` rule and 13b's `link:` rule in a third place: a rule that declines a shape declares the miss rather than quietly resolving it. A link produced here is not a false positive — the repository is right — but it means the oracle is out of date and the test fails loudly rather than silently improving the score.
verdicts.skipped: not a C2 declaration at all, and therefore not something Nerve read and dropped. Recorded here so the oracle states why the count is what it is.

declarations.name: pkg-map
declarations.why: the `.` key of a subpath map, naming a file directly. The neighbour is reached by the repo_id read out of ../pkg-map's own index, and the package name is confirmed against pkg-map's own `name` field before its exports are read at all.

declarations.name: pkg-map/sub
declarations.why: an ordinary subpath key. This is the entity-to-entity link the whole row exists for: host/src/app.ts REFERENCES pkg-map/src/sub.ts.

declarations.name: pkg-map/cond
declarations.why: `import` precedes `require` in the documented order, so src/esm.ts wins over src/cjs.ts. The condition taken is recorded on the link so the choice is auditable rather than implicit.

declarations.name: pkg-map/data
declarations.why: the export entry names a file that is really in pkg-map and that pkg-map's index has never looked at, because .json is not an indexed extension. The link is recorded WITH the path and WITHOUT a target entity id, which is what makes this target_partially_indexed rather than a missing target. Nothing was observed to change there; nothing was observed at all.

declarations.name: pkg-string
declarations.why: `exports` is a single string, which states the `.` subpath and nothing else. host declares the dependency twice — in dependencies and in peerDependencies — and both name the same neighbour, so the one link carries declared_more_than_once rather than a conflict.

declarations.name: pkg-legacy
declarations.why: no `exports` at all, so the legacy fields are read in the documented order. `module` precedes `main`, so src/mod.ts wins over src/main.js; `types` is last and is not reached.

declarations.name: pkg-twin
declarations.why: one specifier, two dependency declarations naming two different repositories, and both of those repositories declare `name: pkg-twin`. Both links are recorded and neither is promoted: picking a winner would be Nerve inventing the answer the manifests declined to give.

declarations.name: pkg-map/only-browser
declarations.why: the entry names only `browser`, which is not one of the three conditions Nerve reads. Choosing it anyway would mean supporting a condition nobody decided to support.

declarations.name: pkg-map/blocked
declarations.why: `null` is a deliberate block written by the package author. It is recorded as one rather than treated as an absence.

declarations.name: pkg-map/escape
declarations.why: the entry resolves to `../../outside.ts`, which leaves the neighbour's root. Refused lexically, before the filesystem is touched, so it is an escape whether or not anything is there.

declarations.name: pkg-string/sub
declarations.why: pkg-string's `exports` is a single string, which states `.` and nothing else. A closed map is a statement about what is not exported.

declarations.name: pkg-legacy/sub
declarations.why: no `exports`, and a subpath. Node would probe the filesystem and guess an extension; that is a resolution rule Nerve would be inventing, so the specifier is declined with the form named.

declarations.name: pkg-map/deep
declarations.why: pkg-map declares `"./*": "./src/*.ts"` and src/deep.ts really is there, so a human reading this manifest would call this a resolved import. Nerve does not expand a pattern into a path, so declining it is a real miss and it is published as one. This is the cost of a gate set for zero false positives, stated rather than bought back by widening the syntax.

declarations.name: pkg-map/gone
declarations.why: the missing-target case. The export entry was read in full and names ./src/gone.ts, which is not in pkg-map's tree. Nothing is claimed about what used to be there, and this is not the same fact as a file the neighbour has and never indexed.

declarations.name: pkg-unregistered
declarations.why: the negative case, and the one that matters most. A real, indexed, adjacent Nerve repository, named by an explicit file: dependency AND imported by name, still produces NO link, because registration is an explicit mutating command and nothing is auto-discovered.

declarations.name: pkg-aliased/thing
declarations.why: host declares `"pkg-aliased": "file:../pkg-map"`, so the dependency key reaches a registered neighbour — and that neighbour declares itself `pkg-map`, not `pkg-aliased`. The third link of the evidence chain is missing, and an alias is a name, and a name is not evidence.

skipped.name: react
skipped.why: the dependency key exists in host/package.json, and its specifier is `^18.2.0`, which C1 declines as a registry range. With no stated path there is no contract for the specifier to travel along, so this is not a C2 declaration at all rather than one that was read and dropped.

skipped.name: ./local
skipped.why: a relative specifier names a file in host itself. Row 1-2 resolves it; it is not a package.
